title: Claude Opus 4.7
content:
## Overview

Claude Opus 4.7 is Anthropic's most capable model as of mid-2026, released in April 2026. It achieves a substantial jump in software engineering and agentic task performance over Opus 4.6, with 3× higher vision resolution and measurable efficiency gains in multi-step workflows — all at the same price as the previous generation.

**Model ID:** `claude-opus-4-7`  
**Pricing:** $5 per million input tokens / $25 per million output tokens (unchanged from Opus 4.6)

---

## Benchmark Performance

### SWE-Bench Verified
Opus 4.7 scores **87.6%** on SWE-Bench Verified, up from 80.8% on Opus 4.6 — a 6.8-point gain. This benchmark tests a model's ability to resolve real GitHub issues from open-source repositories and is the most widely cited measure of coding agent capability.

For context, Gemini 3.1 Pro scores 80.6% and GPT-5.4 scores below Opus 4.7 on this benchmark.

### SWE-Bench Pro
On the more demanding SWE-Bench Pro evaluation, Opus 4.7 scores **64.3%**, up from 53.4% on Opus 4.6 — a nearly 11-point jump. This version tests harder, less frequently solved issues.

| Model | SWE-Bench Verified | SWE-Bench Pro |
|---|---|---|
| Claude Opus 4.7 | **87.6%** | **64.3%** |
| GPT-5.4 | ~84% | 57.7% |
| Gemini 3.1 Pro | 80.6% | 54.2% |
| Claude Opus 4.6 | 80.8% | 53.4% |

### OSWorld-Verified
On OSWorld-Verified, which evaluates computer use ability (operating real desktop GUIs), Opus 4.7 scores **78.0%**, up from 72.7%. This is ahead of GPT-5.4's 75.0%.

---

## Key Improvements

### Vision Resolution
Opus 4.7 receives a **3× upgrade to image input resolution** at the same per-token price. This directly benefits computer use workflows, document analysis, and any task involving screenshots or diagrams.

### Multi-Step Workflow Efficiency
Anthropic reports a **14% improvement in complex multi-step workflow completion** over Opus 4.6, while generating fewer tokens and producing a third fewer tool call errors. In agentic coding contexts, this means less retry overhead and lower API costs for long-running tasks.

### Extended Thinking (`xhigh` Effort)
Opus 4.7 introduces an `xhigh` effort level for extended thinking — beyond the previous `high` setting. This allows the model to allocate substantially more reasoning budget for the hardest problems, at the cost of higher latency and token usage.

---

## Availability

Opus 4.7 is available on:
- **Anthropic API** (`claude-opus-4-7`)
- **Amazon Bedrock**
- **Google Cloud Vertex AI**
- **Microsoft Foundry**

Fast mode in Claude Code uses Opus 4.7 by default (upgraded from Opus 4.6 as of Week 20, May 2026).

---

## When to Use Opus 4.7

- **Production coding agents** requiring high reliability on real-world repositories
- **Long-horizon agentic tasks** with many tool calls (benefits from reduced tool errors)
- **Computer use** workflows needing accurate GUI interaction
- **Complex multi-step reasoning** tasks where the `xhigh` effort level is warranted

For lower-cost, lower-latency use cases, Sonnet 4.6 or Haiku 4.5 remain the appropriate choices.
